title: Visible and invisible (CCC 325–327)
hook: heaven and earth, angels and all that is

segments.voice: Yesterday, providence: God guiding a creation still on its way. Your line was we are co-workers. Did you take your one step? Today, everything that is, seen and unseen. Day one thousand seventy-one.

Take stock of the last minute. Air you can't see went in and out of your lungs. A signal nobody can see probably carried these words to wherever you are. Somewhere, someone's trust in you, which you can't see either, is part of why your day holds together. A lot of what holds a life up is invisible. The Creed said at Sunday Mass calls God the maker of all things visible and invisible. Today we stay with that phrase.
screen: `AIR YOU CAN'T SEE.` → `TRUST YOU CAN'T SEE.` → `ALL THINGS VISIBLE AND INVISIBLE.`

segments.voice: Start with the bigger phrase, heaven and earth. The Catechism says that in scripture it means all that exists: creation as a whole. The earth is the world of people. Heaven can mean the sky, or God's own place, our Father who art in heaven, or the place of the angels around God. Then the Creed adds: visible and invisible. Paul says it in Colossians, in the Douay-Rheims: "in him were all things created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible." A Church council, which the Catechism quotes, put it plainly: from the beginning God made both orders of creation, the spiritual and the bodily, the angelic and the earthly, and then the human, made of both together. Notice where that puts people. In the Catholic picture, human beings stand where the two orders meet: a body, like everything on earth, and a spirit. That's tomorrow's lesson, body and soul. Today, just the frame. Invisible here doesn't mean imaginary. It means real things that eyes can't catch, like the angels and the human soul. The Creed holds that all of creation, seen and unseen, is made by God, and that nothing created sits outside that making. Look back over this week. The faith handed down. Scripture read at four depths. I believe, inside we believe. The Creed's three movements. Power shown as mercy. Providence and its co-workers. And now the maker of all things. That's the carry: seen and unseen. In the Creed's one short phrase, the seen and the unseen stand side by side, on the same list of things made.
screen: `HEAVEN AND EARTH: ALL THAT EXISTS.` · `VISIBLE AND INVISIBLE, IN COLOSSIANS.` · `TWO ORDERS, AND HUMANS MADE OF BOTH.` · `INVISIBLE DOESN'T MEAN IMAGINARY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice something invisible you rely on. Settle, and breathe. Feel the air coming in, cool, then going out, warm. You've never seen it. Now widen out. Name one more invisible thing your life leans on: someone's loyalty, a promise kept, your own memory, a love you've been given. Stay with it. Let it be as real as the chair under you. If you pray, you can thank God, maker of things seen and unseen, for it. If you don't, simply let your attention rest there. The bell holds the time.
Visible and invisible. All that exists, seen and unseen, which the Creed says God made, from the angels to the air. Today's word.
Your line: seen and unseen. Today, keep one small promise nobody would notice if you broke it, an invisible thing you can give. Day one thousand seventy-one.

howItsDone: At Sunday Mass Catholics profess God as maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible, and the Church keeps feasts for the angels in its calendar.

original.note: Greek: the unseen things. Paul's word in Colossians 1:16.

trapdoor: what you thought: invisible things means ghosts and superstition.
what it means: all of creation, including what eyes can't see, like angels and the soul, all made by God.
what a scholar hears: CCC 325–327: heaven and earth as all that exists; Colossians 1:16; a council's teaching on two orders of creation, spiritual and bodily, with the human made of both.

sources.quoted: in him were all things created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible

notes: Catechism paraphrased (copyright): heaven and earth as all that exists; earth the world of men; heaven as firmament, God's 'place', and the place of the angels (CCC 326); the council (Lateran IV, quoted in CCC 327) on both orders of creation and the human made of both. The council is not named or dated in the voice, under the claims rule.
'our Father who art in heaven' is said without quotation marks as a familiar phrase; source listed as Matthew 6:9, paraphrased.
'All things visible and invisible' given as the Creed's phrase at Sunday Mass (Nicene Creed); not placed in quotation marks.
Week-end day (1065–1071): the teach looks back across the week.
Angels are mentioned only briefly; the outline gives them no separate day before 1072. Keeper may want more.
Original: ἀόρατα (Colossians 1:16, τὰ ἀόρατα); confirm accent and pronunciation.

Editor: removed 'God's own life' (and 'truth and love') from the list of invisible things the Creed calls made, a doctrinal error; 'a week spent inside the Creed' fixed, since the week began with tradition and scripture; garbled 'counts both halves' line rewritten; cut 'you've never once doubted it' (telling the listener what they believe); carry changed so it no longer repeats day 1067's 'thank one person'.
Audit: closing line no longer repeats the teach's 'invisible doesn't mean imaginary' a second time.
